newsitem.title: MEXICO: NO MEXICO WORKERS TO BE SPARED PENSION COMMISSIONS.
newsitem.headline: NO MEXICO WORKERS TO BE SPARED PENSION COMMISSIONS.

text.p: Mexico will charge pension commissions even for those insured workers who opt to stay out of the fledgling private pension scheme, the National Retirement Savings Commission (Consar) said on Tuesday.

In an announcement that is likely to draw more fire upon the controversial new pension scheme, Consar said fees will be charged on pensions left in the "Concentrator Account", the alternative for workers who shun private pension firms.
"Due to the operational costs in handling the individual accounts, commissions set by the Consar will be authorized for those workers who are in the Concentrator Account," it said in a statement.

Workers can choose to deposit their retirement savings in one of 17 private firms, known as Afores, or for the next four years after September 17, they can leave them in the Concentrator Account at the central bank to be managed by the government.
Many insured workers have been reluctant to join an Afore because of the steep commissions charged up front -- before they have even begun to recieve returns on their investment.
The Consar said it would set commissions based on prevailing market trends.
((--Henry Tricks, Mexico City newsroom +525 728-9560)) Wednesday, 11 June 1997 02:50:30 ENDS nN10796854
